summary: This version of the farmers' market app refines two of its stream pipelines: the vendor list is now deduplicated and sorted alphabetically, and a vendor's menu is capped at three entries. It shows how `distinct`, `sorted`, and `limit` chain onto a stream to shape the results before they are collected.

lines.text: `Comparator` supplies the ready-made comparison objects used for sorting streams by a chosen field, such as price or name.
Creates the list the whole program works from; the comment below is where the book expects you to add sample products.
Calls the reworked method, which now hands back a `List` in alphabetical order instead of an unordered set.
Storing the vendor name in a variable means the same value is reused for both the menu lookup and the discount calculation, so the two cannot drift apart.
`forEach` with a method reference prints each menu line on its own row, which reads better than printing the list in brackets.
Keeps only organic summer produce, and the `!= null` check guards against a product whose season was never filled in.
Orders the surviving products cheapest first; sorting happens before `map` so the comparator still has full `MarketProduct` objects to inspect.
Transforms each product into just its name, turning a stream of products into a stream of strings.
Gathers the streamed values back into an ordinary `List` that the caller can print or loop over.
Drops missing or empty vendor names so blanks do not appear in the finished list.
Removes duplicate vendor names, which is what gives this list the uniqueness a `Set` used to provide.
Sorts the remaining names alphabetically using each string's natural order, satisfying the request for a sorted vendor list.
Selects only this vendor's products, and `equalsIgnoreCase` means a difference in capitalization will not hide a match.
A commented-out sort left in place as a reminder: uncomment it to take the first three items alphabetically rather than in list order.
Builds a display string for each product, with `%.2f` forcing prices to show exactly two decimal places like real money.
Stops the pipeline after three results, so the printed menu stays short no matter how many products the vendor has.
